subject: Workplace Skills
title: Confirmation Bias in Decisions
description: One-minute skill: Confirmation Bias in Decisions.

hook.text: Kodak's engineers showed leadership digital photography in 1975. Leadership sought data that film would survive.

buildup.text: Confirmation bias means seeking information that supports what you already believe and ignoring contradictions.

discovery.text: This bias is strongest when the belief is tied to identity or past decisions. Admitting error feels like failure.

twist.text: Smart people are not immune. Higher intelligence just makes you better at rationalizing what you want to believe.

climax.text: Assign a devil's advocate in every major decision. Actively search for evidence that proves you wrong.

punchline.text: Seek disconfirming evidence. It saves you from yourself.

quiz.question: Why are intelligent people not immune to confirmation bias?
options: Intelligence is unrelated to decision-making quality
Higher intelligence makes people better at rationalizing existing beliefs
They simply encounter fewer situations requiring critical thinking
